newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk leftist party wins Is Bank case.
newsitem.headline: Turk leftist party wins Is Bank case.

text.p: A Turkish leftist party won a court case against the Treasury on Thursday enabling it to take over 20 percent of shares in T. Is Bankasi A.S., one of the country's largest commercial banks.

State-run Anatolian news agency said the Republican People's Party (CHP) will under the ruling gain control of 19.8 percent of the bank's shares, which had been owned by the founder of modern Turkey and the CHP, Mustafa Kemal Ataturk.

"As a result of the case heard in the Ankara Commercial Court today, the decision was given that Ataturk's shares be passed on to the CHP," the CHP's lawyer Erbasar Ozsoy was quoted as saying by Anatolian.
It said an 8.2 percent stake of the bank's shares owned by Ataturk had already been transferred to the CHP.
After Thursday's verdict 45 percent of the bank's shares were held by the bank's pension fund, 28 percent by the CHP, 15 percent by third parties and 12 percent by the Treasury, it said.
The CHP was created by Ataturk in 1923 and was reformed in 1992 after being banned 12 years earlier in a military coup.
